newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New Russian Eurobond delayed by 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: New Russian Eurobond delayed by 1997 budget.

text.p: Russia's planned follow-up Eurobond is being held up by delays in passing the 1997 budget but the government is considering offers from banks to lead-manage the issue, a Finance Ministry official said on Wednesday.

"The budget is in some sense delaying the new issue," Vladimir Dmitriyev, deputy head of the foreign credits department, told Reuters. "We cannot move the corresponding documents through the government."

The Federation Council upper house of parliament is likely to debate the 1997 budget on February 12. Once the council has passed the budget it must still be signed by President Boris Yeltsin to become law.
The State Duma lower house approved the budget last week.
Dmitriyev said analysts had recommended Russia to make the new issue in marks, but a decision had not yet been taken.

"Judging by the current state of the market a mark Eurobond would be preferable. Analysts say borrowing in dollars is not profitable now," he said. "But we cannot rule out the possibility that the situation will change."
Dmitriyev said the government was considering various options as an alternative to mark paper, including both dollars and other currencies.

Russia launched its debut $1.00 billion five-year Eurobond last November. Government officials have said the next issue will be launched in the first quarter of 1997 and Russia planned to raise a total of $1.5 billion in 1997.
